# 1 Kings Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** And-Rehoboam went to-Shechem, for to-Shechem all Israel had-come to-make-him-king.

**2** And-it-was when-Jeroboam son-of Nebat heard — and-he was still in-Egypt, where he-had-fled from-before the-king Solomon, and-Jeroboam dwelt in-Egypt —

**3** and-they-sent and-called-him. And-Jeroboam and-all the-assembly-of Israel came and-spoke to-Rehoboam, saying,

**4** "Your-father made-heavy ʾet-our-yoke. And-you now, lighten the-hard service-of your-father and-ʾet-his-heavy yoke that he-put upon-us, and-we-will-serve-you."

**5** And-he-said to-them, "Go — yet three days — and-return to-me." And-the-people went.

**6** And-the-king Rehoboam consulted with the-elders who had-been standing before Solomon his-father while-he-was-alive, saying, "How do-you advise to-return a-word to-this people?"

**7** And-they-spoke to-him, saying, "If today you-will-be a-servant to-this people and-serve-them and-answer-them and-speak to-them good words, then-they-will-be servants to-you all the-days."

**8** But-he-forsook ʾet-the-counsel-of the-elders that they-counseled-him, and-he-consulted with the-young-men who had-grown-up with-him, who-stood before-him.

**9** And-he-said to-them, "What do-you advise, and-we-will-return a-word to-this people who-spoke to-me, saying, 'Lighten the-yoke that your-father put upon-us'?"

**10** And-the-young-men who had-grown-up with-him spoke to-him, saying, "Thus you-shall-say to-this people who-spoke to-you, saying, 'Your-father made-heavy our-yoke, but-you lighten it for-us' — thus you-shall-speak to-them: 'My-little-finger is-thicker than-my-father's loins.

**11** And-now, my-father loaded upon-you a-heavy yoke, and-I will-add to your-yoke. My-father disciplined-you with-whips, but-I will-discipline-you with-scorpions.'"

**12** And-Jeroboam and-all the-people came to-Rehoboam on-the-third day, as the-king had-spoken, saying, "Return to-me on-the-third day."

**13** And-the-king answered ʾet-the-people harshly, and-forsook ʾet-the-counsel-of the-elders that they-counseled-him.

**14** And-he-spoke to-them according-to-the-counsel-of the-young-men, saying, "My-father made-heavy your-yoke, and-I will-add to your-yoke. My-father disciplined-you with-whips, but-I will-discipline-you with-scorpions."

**15** And-the-king did-not listen to the-people, for it-was a-turning from YHWH, so-that he-might-establish ʾet-his-word that YHWH spoke by-the-hand-of Ahijah the-Shilonite to-Jeroboam son-of Nebat.

**16** And-all Israel saw that the-king did-not listen to-them, and-the-people returned the-king a-word, saying, "What portion have-we in-David? And-there-is-no inheritance in-the-son-of Jesse! To-your-tents, Israel! Now see-to your-own-house, David!" And-Israel went to-their-tents.

**17** And-the-sons-of Israel who-dwelt in-the-cities-of Judah — Rehoboam reigned over-them.

**18** And-the-king Rehoboam sent ʾet-Adoram, who was over the-forced-labor, and-all Israel stoned-him with-stones, and-he-died. And-the-king Rehoboam made-haste to-go-up into-the-chariot, to-flee to-Jerusalem.

**19** And-Israel rebelled against the-house-of David to this day.

**20** And-it-was when-all Israel heard that Jeroboam had-returned, and-they-sent and-called-him to the-assembly, and-they-made-him-king over all Israel. None followed the-house-of David except the-tribe-of Judah alone.

**21** And-Rehoboam came to-Jerusalem, and-he-assembled ʾet-all the-house-of Judah and-ʾet-the-tribe-of Benjamin — a-hundred and-eighty thousand chosen men, makers-of war — to-fight against the-house-of Israel, to-return the-kingdom to-Rehoboam son-of Solomon.

**22** And-the-word-of God came to-Shemaiah the-man-of God, saying,

**23** "Say to-Rehoboam son-of Solomon, king-of Judah, and-to all the-house-of Judah and-Benjamin, and-to the-rest-of the-people, saying,

**24** 'Thus says YHWH: You-shall-not go-up, and-you-shall-not fight against your-brothers the-sons-of Israel. Return each-man to-his-house, for from-me this thing has-happened.'" And-they-heard ʾet-the-word-of YHWH and-returned to-go, according-to-the-word-of YHWH.

**25** And-Jeroboam built ʾet-Shechem in-the-hill-country-of Ephraim and-dwelt in-it. And-he-went-out from-there and-built ʾet-Penuel.

**26** And-Jeroboam said in-his-heart, "Now the-kingdom will-return to-the-house-of David.

**27** If this people goes-up to-make sacrifices in-the-house-of YHWH in-Jerusalem, then-the-heart-of this people will-return to their-lord, to-Rehoboam king-of Judah, and-they-will-kill-me, and-return to Rehoboam king-of Judah."

**28** And-the-king took-counsel, and-made two calves-of gold. And-he-said to-them, "Too-much for-you, going-up to-Jerusalem. Behold your-gods, Israel, who brought-you-up from-the-land-of Egypt!"

**29** And-he-set ʾet-the-one in-Bethel, and-ʾet-the-one he-put in-Dan.

**30** And-this thing became a-sin, and-the-people went before the-one, to Dan.

**31** And-he-made ʾet-a-house-of high-places, and-he-made priests from-the-ends-of the-people who were not from-the-sons-of Levi.

**32** And-Jeroboam made a-feast in-the-eighth month, on-the-fifteenth day-of the-month, like the-feast that was in-Judah, and-he-went-up upon the-altar. So he-did in-Bethel, to-sacrifice to-the-calves that he-made. And-he-placed in-Bethel ʾet-the-priests-of the-high-places that he-made.

**33** And-he-went-up upon the-altar that he-made in-Bethel on-the-fifteenth day in-the-eighth month, in-the-month that he-devised from-his-own-heart. And-he-made a-feast for-the-sons-of Israel, and-went-up upon the-altar to-burn-incense.

---
## EMET Textual Notes

1. **12:4 — "your-father made-heavy our-yoke"**: The word mas (forced labor) from 4:6, 5:13, 9:15 now returns as the grievance that tears the kingdom. Solomon's building program was a debt that came due under his son.

2. **12:10 — "my-little-finger is-thicker than-my-father's loins"**: The crudest political boast in the Hebrew Bible. The young men's advice turns governance into a contest of masculine dominance.

3. **12:15 — "a-turning from YHWH"**: The narrator's theological interpretation: Rehoboam's folly was divinely orchestrated to fulfill Ahijah's prophecy. Human foolishness serves divine purpose.

4. **12:16 — "What portion have-we in-David?"**: The cry of secession. These words echo Sheba's rebellion (2 Sam 20:1) and represent the permanent fracture of the Davidic state.

5. **12:28 — "Behold your-gods"**: The golden calves deliberately echo Aaron's words at Sinai (Exod 32:4). Jeroboam recreates Israel's foundational sin as official state religion.

— EMET
